title: Create a deterministic machine-legible building-code representation
description: Downstream systems needed stable code structure that could be compared, referenced, validated, and traced back to a specific publication, rather than a search result or prose summary.
author: bcast

title: Treat search, RAG, or summarization as the code representation
description: A retrieval or summary layer could answer questions quickly, but it could not provide deterministic hierarchy, stable identities, exact source spans, or reproducible structural comparisons.
author: bcast

title: Downstream code analysis needs addressable provisions, not merely relevant passages
description: Building Code Map, edition comparison, amendment overlays, and future reasoning require provisions with durable location and provenance so retrieval does not become authority.
author: bcast

title: Build a staged compiler rather than a search index
description: The repository would transform source artifacts into publication structure and then selected semantic representations, while preserving unsupported or ambiguous language instead of inventing meaning.
author: bcast

title: Building Code AST became a source-structure and evidence layer
description: The project owns deterministic source structure and parser evidence. Retrieval, jurisdiction selection, and compliance conclusions remain downstream concerns.
author: bcast

title: Separate technical representation from legal authority
description: An AST can identify and transform an edition, but it does not make the derived structure authoritative, establish adoption, or replace official text and AHJ judgment.
author: bcast

title: Represent publication structure before interpreting rule meaning
description: The initial provision parser proved exact semantic spans were possible, but it could not express chapters, nested lists, definitions, tables, or document-level hierarchy.
author: bcast

title: A provision-first AST could not carry full document organization
description: Modality, threshold, action, and exception fields were useful for a bounded sentence, yet document ingestion required a separate tree that did not prematurely assign semantics.
author: bcast

title: Put publication hierarchy and interpreted rule meaning in one universal tree
description: This would make every structural parser imply semantic correctness and force code-family layout facts into a meaning-oriented schema.
author: bcast

title: Create an independently versioned Document AST
description: The Document AST records source artifact, edition, recursive structural nodes, stable identities, exact spans, and diagnostics while excluding modality, conditions, actions, and compliance fields.
author: bcast

title: Derive node identity from artifact, edition, node type, and structural locator
description: Stable identifiers survive reparsing of the same edition while changing when the publication identity changes; source text and offsets remain evidence rather than identity inputs.
author: bcast

title: Shared document primitives became the neutral contract
description: Document, chapter, section, subsection, paragraph, list item, definition entry, table parts, headings, notes, footnotes, and unsupported structures form the common vocabulary without claiming a common grammar.
author: bcast

title: Recover printed structure from imperfect PDF evidence
description: Source PDFs expose text, coordinates, outlines, and visual layout unevenly. The parser needed to retain enough evidence to reconstruct reading order without confusing extraction order with code hierarchy.
author: bcast

title: Treat the PDF text stream as document hierarchy
description: Headers, footers, columns, continuation pages, glyph runs, and table fragments made text order an unreliable proxy for printed or logical hierarchy.
author: bcast

title: Coordinates and reading order are evidence, not the final tree
description: NEC required two-column block ordering and article boundaries; IBC exposed glyph-level spacing, superscripts, mixed table-and-column bands, and recurring page furniture.
author: bcast

title: Infer hierarchy from font size or indentation alone
description: Visual style helps identify candidates but cannot safely distinguish continuations, wrapped titles, list levels, columns, or publisher furniture across editions.
author: bcast

title: Preserve page, geometry, extraction span, and exclusion evidence
description: Layout adapters retain source coordinates and normalized character spans so every structural claim can be audited against the source region that produced it.
author: bcast

title: Keep ambiguous or unsupported layout as diagnostics instead of discarding it
description: Unknown table boundaries, malformed markers, and unresolved reading order remain visible evidence. Successful extraction is never inferred from silent omission.
author: bcast

title: Use the supplied 2017 NEC PDF to exercise real code ingestion
description: The first real source slice had to prove local, source-safe ingestion, exact article boundaries, provenance, and deterministic private outputs without publishing licensed text.
author: bcast

title: Keep NEC source artifacts and text-bearing outputs local
description: The public repository contains parser code, schemas, tests, and documentation; PDFs, extracted prose, page images, source hashes, and generated ArticleSeeds remain private.
author: bcast

title: Validate Articles 90, 100, and 110 before claiming broader coverage
description: The initial production slice exercised scope and language policy, definitions, general requirements, exceptions, notes, and one table-like region while keeping whole-edition support out of scope.
author: bcast

title: Build source-bound private NEC ArticleSeeds
description: The optional PyMuPDF adapter discovers article bookmarks, trims same-page transitions, orders blocks, emits source maps, and validates Document AST spans.
author: bcast

title: Fragment review exposed article transitions, definition candidates, and table-like blocks
description: Production smoke tests and later selected-fragment review corrected boundaries and classifications that synthetic fixtures alone could not reveal.
author: bcast

title: NEC 2017 support is real but intentionally bounded
description: Main supports local ingestion and hierarchy/semantic processing for the exercised selected articles. It does not claim every article, table, figure, annex, or edition.
author: bcast

title: Reconstruct NEC articles, parts, sections, subdivisions, lists, notes, and exceptions
description: Flat ArticleSeed blocks were not enough for stable locators, parent-child validation, selected semantic review, or clause comparison.
author: bcast

title: PDF blocks merge and split NEC clauses differently from printed hierarchy
description: Titled subdivisions may share blocks; repeated marker classes can recur at different depths; Article 100 parentheticals can resemble list markers.
author: bcast

title: Treat every parenthetical marker as a universal hierarchy token
description: The same syntax can represent structural subdivisions, ordinary lists, units, or definition text, and marker meaning changes with context and edition.
author: bcast

title: Use NEC-specific hierarchy rules with contextual evidence
description: The hierarchy builder uses Part and Section identities, title evidence, list introductions, marker ancestry, source order, and ambiguity diagnostics rather than syntax alone.
author: bcast

title: Use the prior junk-drawer NEC hierarchy as a conformance oracle, not a dependency
description: The private reference validates parser output and reveals mismatches but does not repair output, enter generated artifacts, or become required at runtime.
author: bcast

title: Use edition-aware NEC Style Manual profiles as parser priors and validation context
description: Style guidance helps interpret definition placement, parallel numbering, titles, and note identity, but the published edition remains source evidence and ambiguous markers remain unresolved.
author: bcast

title: Selected NEC hierarchy matched the independent oracle without runtime coupling
description: The reviewed Article 90 and 110 structural records matched the local oracle; Article 100 produced no false numbered-clause records in that comparison.
author: bcast

title: Preserve clause context before deriving normative meaning
description: Meaning depends on ownership, order, exceptions, conditions, definitions, references, and surrounding source, not just the sentence containing a modal verb.
author: bcast

title: Printed hierarchy, logical hierarchy, and normative dependency are not identical
description: A continuation paragraph may belong to a printed clause; an exception can modify an ancestor; a definition or table can govern distant provisions through references.
author: bcast
